name: Ishmael the son of Nethaniah
charge: Murder of Gedaliah the governor at his own table; slaughter of the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and of seventy pilgrims
summary: Of the seed royal, hired by the king of the Ammonites, Ishmael ate bread with Gedaliah at Mizpah and killed him, then killed the men with him, then killed seventy mourners on their way to the house of the Lord and threw them in a pit. He escaped to Ammon with eight men. Scripture records no sentence on him; it records what his deed cost the remnant.
offense: Ishmael came with ten men to Gedaliah at Mizpah and ate with him. During that hospitality he rose up and killed the governor appointed over the remnant, together with Jews and Chaldeans there. Gedaliah had previously refused to believe the warning of a plot against his life. Ishmael then went out weeping to meet eighty men coming with offerings to the house of the Lord. He drew them into Mizpah and killed seventy, casting their bodies into a pit. Ten were spared when they offered hidden stores of food. He took the remaining people captive and set out toward the Ammonites. His tears concealed violence, and the prospect of supplies determined whom he spared.
judgment: Johanan and the captains pursued Ishmael. The captives rejoiced when they saw them and returned with Johanan, while Ishmael escaped to the Ammonites with eight men. The account records the breaking of his hold over the captives, but not his eventual death or a further punishment. His bloodshed left the remnant afraid of Babylonian retaliation and helped set the stage for their flight toward Egypt. His escape did not make his murders lawful, nor did it erase the injury done to a people already reduced by war.

verses.text: Moreover Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were in the fields, came to Gedaliah to Mizpah,
And said unto him, Dost thou certainly know that Baalis the king of the Ammonites hath sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay thee? But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam believed them not.

Then Johanan the son of Kareah spake to Gedaliah in Mizpah secretly, saying, Let me go, I pray thee, and I will slay Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and no man shall know it: wherefore should he slay thee, that all the Jews which are gathered unto thee should be scattered, and the remnant in Judah perish?
But Gedaliah the son of Ahikam said unto Johanan the son of Kareah, Thou shalt not do this thing: for thou speakest falsely of Ishmael.

Now it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, and the princes of the king, even ten men with him, came unto Gedaliah the son of Ahikam to Mizpah; and there they did eat bread together in Mizpah.

Then arose Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and the ten men that were with him, and smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam the son of Shaphan with the sword, and slew him, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the land.
Ishmael also slew all the Jews that were with him, even with Gedaliah, at Mizpah, and the Chaldeans that were found there, and the men of war.
And it came to pass the second day after he had slain Gedaliah, and no man knew it,

That there came certain from Shechem, from Shiloh, and from Samaria, even fourscore men, having their beards shaven, and their clothes rent, and having cut themselves, with offerings and incense in their hand, to bring them to the house of the Lord.
And Ishmael the son of Nethaniah went forth from Mizpah to meet them, weeping all along as he went: and it came to pass, as he met them, he said unto them, Come to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam.
And it was so, when they came into the midst of the city, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah slew them, and cast them into the midst of the pit, he, and the men that were with him.

But ten men were found among them that said unto Ishmael, Slay us not: for we have treasures in the field, of wheat, and of barley, and of oil, and of honey. So he forbare, and slew them not among their brethren.

Now the pit wherein Ishmael had cast all the dead bodies of the men, whom he had slain because of Gedaliah, was it which Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah filled it with them that were slain.

Then Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people that were in Mizpah, even the king’s daughters, and all the people that remained in Mizpah, whom Nebuzar–adan the captain of the guard had committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam: and Ishmael the son of Nethaniah carried them away captive, and departed to go over to the Ammonites.
But when Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, heard of all the evil that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had done,
Then they took all the men, and went to fight with Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, and found him by the great waters that are in Gibeon.
Now it came to pass, that when all the people which were with Ishmael saw Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, then they were glad.
So all the people that Ishmael had carried away captive from Mizpah cast about and returned, and went unto Johanan the son of Kareah.
But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah escaped from Johanan with eight men, and went to the Ammonites.

Then took Johanan the son of Kareah, and all the captains of the forces that were with him, all the remnant of the people whom he had recovered from Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, from Mizpah, after that he had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, even mighty men of war, and the women, and the children, and the eunuchs, whom he had brought again from Gibeon:
And they departed, and dwelt in the habitation of Chimham, which is by Beth–lehem, to go to enter into Egypt,
Because of the Chaldeans: for they were afraid of them, because Ishmael the son of Nethaniah had slain Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon made governor in the land.

But it came to pass in the seventh month, that Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, the son of Elishama, of the seed royal, came, and ten men with him, and smote Gedaliah, that he died, and the Jews and the Chaldees that were with him at Mizpah.
And all the people, both small and great, and the captains of the armies, arose, and came to Egypt: for they were afraid of the Chaldees.
Whoso sheddeth man’s blood, by man shall his blood be shed: for in the image of God made he man.

entries.commentary: The word came to Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard let him go from Ramah, where he had been bound in chains among all the captives of Jerusalem and Judah being carried away to Babylon; Jeremiah was let go when Jerusalem was seized. The captain, a heathen, told Jeremiah that the Most High had pronounced this evil upon the place because the people sinned against Him and would not obey His voice, so this thing had come upon them. The nations always knew why we went into captivity; it is sin, the breaking of the Most High's laws, that becomes our weakness and how we are overcome. -

The captain loosed Jeremiah from the chains on his hands and gave him an ultimatum, either to come with him to Babylon where he would be looked after well, or to remain in the land as he pleased. He directed Jeremiah to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, whom the king of Babylon had made governor over the cities of Judah, gave him food and a reward, and let him go; Gedaliah was one of Jeremiah's good friends. Jeremiah went to Gedaliah at Mizpah and dwelt with him among the people left in the land.

When all the captains of the forces in the fields heard that the king of Babylon had made Gedaliah governor and had committed to him the men, women, children, and the poor of the land who were not carried away, they came together to him at Mizpah. Gedaliah swore to them not to fear serving the Chaldeans but to dwell in the land, gather wine and summer fruits and oil, and serve the king of Babylon, and it would be well with them; the war was over and they were already conquered. All the Jews scattered in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and the other countries heard of the remnant left under Gedaliah and returned to the land of Judah, gathering wine and summer fruits in abundance.

Johanan the son of Kareah and the captains of the forces came to Gedaliah at Mizpah and warned him that Baalis the king of the Ammonites had sent Ishmael the son of Nethaniah to slay him, but Gedaliah believed them not. Johanan spoke secretly to Gedaliah, offering to kill Ishmael himself so that Gedaliah would not be slain and the gathered remnant scattered. Gedaliah forbade Johanan to do it, saying he spoke falsely of Ishmael, and refused to believe the plot.

In the seventh month Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed and a prince of the king, came with ten men to Gedaliah at Mizpah, and they ate bread together at a banquet held in Ishmael's honor. Ishmael and his ten men rose up and smote Gedaliah the son of Ahikam with the sword and slew him, the governor the king of Babylon had made over the land. Ishmael also slew all the Jews with Gedaliah at Mizpah and the Chaldeans and men of war that were found there.

The second day after the murder, before anyone knew of it, eighty men came from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria with their beards shaven, their clothes rent, and their bodies cut, bringing offerings and incense to the house of the Most High. Ishmael went out from Mizpah weeping as he met them, playing a part, and invited them in to Gedaliah; when they came into the midst of the city he and his men slew them and cast them into a pit. Ten of the eighty were spared when they told Ishmael they had hidden treasures of wheat, barley, oil, and honey in the field. The pit Ishmael filled with the slain was the one Asa the king had made for fear of Baasha king of Israel during the war between them. -

Ishmael carried away captive all the residue of the people at Mizpah, including the king's daughters, whom Nebuzaradan had committed to Gedaliah, and departed toward the Ammonites. When Johanan and the captains heard of all the evil Ishmael had done, not only killing Gedaliah but at least eighty other men, they took their men and went to fight him and found him by the great waters in Gibeon. All the people Ishmael had taken captive were glad to see Johanan, turned about, and returned to him, but Ishmael escaped from Johanan with eight men and went to the Ammonites.

Johanan took the whole remnant he had recovered from Ishmael, the mighty men of war, the women, the children, and the eunuchs, and departed to dwell near Bethlehem on the way toward Egypt. They set out to seek refuge in Egypt because they were afraid of the Chaldeans, since Ishmael had slain Gedaliah whom the king of Babylon had made governor; with Gedaliah dead they felt they had no reason to stay.

In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign Nebuchadnezzar came with all his host against Jerusalem, pitched against it, and built forts round about it. The city was besieged until the eleventh year of Zedekiah, and the famine prevailed in the city. Because the city was besieged no food, water, or goods could get in, so there was no bread for the people of the land.

The city was broken up and the men of war fled by night by the way of the gate between two walls by the king's garden, while the Chaldeans were round about the city. The army pursued the king, overtook him in the plains of Jericho, and his army was scattered from him, and they took him to the king of Babylon at Riblah, where judgment was given upon him. They slew Zedekiah's sons before his eyes, then put out his eyes, bound him with fetters of brass, and carried him to Babylon, just as Jeremiah had warned him.

In the fifth month of the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard came to Jerusalem. He burnt the house of the Lord, the king's house, and every great man's house, and the army broke down the walls of Jerusalem round about. He carried away the rest of the people and the fugitives, but left the poor of the land to be vinedressers and husbandmen, since the poor could not fend for themselves.

The Chaldeans broke in pieces the pillars of brass, the bases, and the brasen sea that were in the house of the Lord, and carried the brass to Babylon because it was valuable. They took away the pots, shovels, snuffers, spoons, and vessels of brass, and the firepans and bowls of gold and silver the captain of the guard took away. The two pillars, one sea, and the bases Solomon had made were of brass without weight, the one pillar eighteen cubits high with a brasen chapiter, wreathen work, and pomegranates round about.

The captain of the guard took Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and the three keepers of the door. He took an officer over the men of war, five men in the king's presence, the principal scribe of the host, and threescore men of the people found in the city. Nebuzaradan brought them to the king of Babylon at Riblah, and the king smote and slew them there; so Judah was carried away out of their land.

Over the people left in the land Nebuchadnezzar made Gedaliah the son of Ahikam, the son of Shaphan, governor. Gedaliah counselled the captains and their men not to fear to serve the Chaldeans but to dwell in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it would be well with them. But Ishmael the son of Nethaniah, of the royal seed, came with ten men and smote Gedaliah and the Jews and Chaldeans with him, and the people fled to Egypt for fear of the Chaldeans, killing a man who gave wise counsel.

In the thirty seventh year of the captivity of Jehoiachin, Evilmerodach king of Babylon lifted up his head out of prison and spake kindly to him. He set his throne above the thrones of the other kings in Babylon, changed his prison garments, and let him eat bread continually before him all the days of his life. Jehoiachin was given a continual daily allowance for the rest of his life, a mercy shown at the very end of the account. --- Topics: [Idolatry](/encyclopedia/idolatry) · [Sacrifice and Atonement](/encyclopedia/sacrifice-and-atonement) · [The Covenant](/encyclopedia/the-covenant) · [The Feasts of the Most High](/encyclopedia/the-feasts-of-the-most-high) · [The Priesthood](/encyclopedia/the-priesthood)
Noah and his sons were told to replenish the earth after the flood, and the earth is replenished with righteous children; a multitude of ungodly children profits nothing.
The fear and dread of man upon the beasts is not how it was in the beginning, and not how it will remain; the original relationship between man and the animals will be restored.

This is the introduction of man eating meat. The Most High did not give man a new stomach; the body was already made for it and it lay dormant until after the flood. Having the liberty to eat meat does not mean eating without balance; be not too greedy upon meats, for excess of meats brings sickness. The law of what may be eaten was already understood; you could not eat everything. The doctrine that says you can pray over anything and eat it is a seducing spirit and a doctrine of devils. Fish is meat; all flesh is not the same flesh, but the flesh of beasts, of fishes, and of birds are all flesh. Every creature of God is good for what it was made for, and it is sanctified by the word of God, and the word that sanctifies what may be eaten is the dietary law.
The law against eating flesh with the blood was given to Adam and is still in place with Noah; the word is true from the beginning.

The Most High requiring blood at the hand of every beast is animal sacrifice, still in place with Noah, passed down generation to generation. The judgment for sin has always been death. When Eve sinned and caused Adam to sin, either they had to die, or something had to stand in their place; the blood of the animal stood in for them. That is the scapegoat: it takes the wrongdoings, mistakes, and faults of others and places them on the animal. That is why Cain and Abel were bringing offerings, because they knew of the sacrifice from [Genesis 3](/bible/genesis/3).

Whoso sheddeth man's blood, by man shall his blood be shed: life for life. This law is way before Moses, so it cannot be dismissed as the law of Moses. The laws were never done away with; Christ came not to destroy the law but to fulfil, and not one jot or tittle passes from the law.

The covenant established here is with Noah, his seed, and every living creature: all flesh shall never again be cut off by the waters of a flood. This is a general covenant with all flesh. The covenant with Israel is found in [Jeremiah 31](/bible/jeremiah/31).

The bow in the cloud, the rainbow, is the token of the covenant between the Most High and the earth; it compasses the heaven about with a glorious circle, and His hands bended it. The world has taken that same bow, the token of the covenant, and turned it into the symbol of sodomy. The spiritual eyes will see what that means: the great city is spiritually called Sodom and Egypt.
The waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh. The next time the destruction is not water but fire, when the day of the Lord comes and the elements melt with fervent heat.

Shem, Ham, and Japheth went forth out of the ark and the whole earth was overspread from them. Ham dwelt in what is called Africa; Shem in the land mass toward Arabia; Japheth went into Europe. Ham is the father of Canaan, and Canaan dwelt in the land later called the land of Israel. That is how you know the land of Israel is a part of Africa; the maps separate Israel from Africa so that the connection is not made.

Noah was still perfect and righteous. A just man falleth seven times and riseth up again; one fall does not undo righteousness. Understand Noah's heart: he preached repentance for around a hundred years, and everyone he knew outside his house drowned. Strong drink is for him that is ready to perish and wine for those of heavy hearts; Noah drank too much, but he remained righteous in the eyes of the Most High. Ham saw the nakedness of his father and did not cover him; Shem and Japheth went backward and covered their father without looking. The commandments concerning nakedness were being applied; [Leviticus 18](/bible/leviticus/18) opens those laws.

Noah was asleep, so how did he know what his younger son had done? The Most High speaks to man in a dream, in a vision of the night, and reveals His secret unto His servants the prophets; Noah was a preacher of righteousness, and the Lord told him. Cursed be Canaan: a servant of servants unto his brethren. Blessed be the Lord God of Shem: it was revealed that the Messiah and the righteous seed would come through Shem.
